To harvest Facebook ground truth, we have monitored Facebook comments under personality test results released on the 16personalities portal (see Figure 1B for an example). The vendor is named exactly once, as a place where results were released. So on a sentence-level reading the code is C0, which is what I recorded. E1 is coded because the Natijalar (Results) section reports, in definite past tense, that lessons based on Multiple Intelligences and MBTI were conducted and that students 'who came to know their personal learning styles through the MBTI test' developed strategies, and separately reports extravert vs. introvert students showing differentiated outcomes -- read together, this is the work's own account that respondents completed a personality instrument (the §2 gate for E1). A stricter reading is defensible: some adjacent quantitative claims in the same Natijalar section are sourced to secondary literature rather than the author's own data (e.g., the 25% figure is followed by '(Dunn & Dunn, 2000)'), and the Xulosa va tavsiyalar (Recommendations) section recommends beginning to use the 16personalities.com free test 'har semestr boshida' (at the start of each semester) as a step for the future, which sits in tension with the Results section already reporting outcomes attributed to its use. So it is not certain that any primary data collection by this author occurred, and E4 (a position/advocacy piece written in results-report style) cannot be ruled out from the text alone. Separately, the instrument code (a) rests on Level-2 evidence only: the Kirish sentence identifies 'MBTI' with 'this free personality-determination test' at the 16personalities.com URL, and that identification is reused consistently (Discussion, Recommendations) -- but no sentence anywhere states explicitly that respondents completed that specific URL/test for the study reported in Natijalar. The (a) code is an inference from the paper's own undifferentiated, conflated use of 'MBTI' and the vendor's free test as one thing, not a direct Methods statement of what was administered. || c2: Two linked judgements, both at a boundary the protocol does not settle. (1) E1 vs E4. The work has no Methods, Participants or Data Collection section, no sample size, no site, no dates and no design; the case for administration rests entirely on the past-tense Natijalar (Results) section — "Ushbu tadqiqot davomida ... olib borilgan darslar", "MBTI testi orqali shaxsiy o‘quv uslublarini bilgan talabalar ... ishlab chiqdi", and extravert/introvert outcome contrasts — plus unsourced figures ("Talabalarning darsga jalb qilinishi 30-40% ga oshdi"). Read as a genuine account of teaching in which students took the test, the work is E1; read as a position/review piece with a narrative results section that reports no type data of its own, it is E4 and the instrument code drops. §2 is explicit that failure to describe provenance is the finding rather than a reason to exclude, so I coded E1, but the reading is thin and an adjudicator could reasonably rule E4. (2) If E1 stands, (a) vs (c) c-online. The work never says in so many words "respondents completed the 16Personalities test": it says the MBTI test was used and, in three places in the body (Kirish, Muhokama, Xulosa), identifies that free test with https://www.16personalities.com/free-personality-test. §4.1 does not apply — the vendor URL is in the running text, not only in the reference list, so c-vendor-cited-only is not the shape here — and §4.3's principle that the URL decides, together with §3.2's "described free/online test whose cited URL resolves to the vendor's domain", gives (a) at hierarchy level 2. A stricter reader who required an explicit administration sentence would code (c) c-online. Coded (a) at level 2 rather than level 1 because the work has no Methods section at all.
free_text: c2: The retrieved file holds one work only — the assigned paper, pp. 157-166 of the Termiz State Pedagogical Institute conference proceedings (17-18 April 2026), with its own three-language abstract, sections (Kirish / Adabiyotlar tahlili / Muhokama / Natijalar / Xulosa va tavsiyalar) and a 17-entry reference list, so §3.6's several-works-in-one-file rule is not triggered and no neighbouring work's sentences were used. text_is_abstract is false: this is a full proceedings paper (~3,200 words), not a conference abstract, although its venue is a conference proceedings volume rather than a journal. Two observations the coded fields cannot hold. (i) Reference 15 credits the 16Personalities URL to "Humanmetrics.com. (2015)" — the vendor page is filed under a different vendor's name and dated to a year, i.e. the only formal citation of the instrument is wrong about who publishes it. (ii) The paper's title announces "raqamli geymifikatsiya platformalari" (digital gamification platforms), and the body never discusses gamification at all; the title matches the assigned record exactly, so this is a property of the work, not a mismatch of the retrieved text. No second instrument is administered and there is no non-human arm; the Multiple Intelligences component is a framework, not an administered personality instrument.

title: Persönlichkeitstests im beruflichen Kontext
quote_e: "It is based on a critical narrative review of scientific literature, test manuals, and publicly available information provided by test publishers, supplemented by experience gained from their practical use in organizations." — Abstract (English)
uncertain_note: c2: Three things the protocol does not cleanly decide here. (1) Input: §1 requires the full text, not the abstract, and codes a work whose full text cannot be obtained as 'unobtainable'. What was retrieved is the Zenodo landing page containing the German and English abstracts and repository metadata; the article PDF was not retrieved. This record may belong in 'unobtainable' rather than being coded, but that value has no slot in this schema, so it is coded as instructed with text_is_abstract set true (§3.6, which is worded for conference abstracts rather than repository landing pages). All R and C coding below rests on the two abstract sentences that contain a 16Personalities word form; R4 in particular could exist in the unretrieved PDF and cannot be ruled out from this text. (2) R6's wording ('named in passing; no claim in the work rests on it') fits awkwardly: 16Personalities is a named object of the review, not a passing mention, yet none of R1-R5 describes the work's own use of the vendor, and §5 as amended attaches a flag to the citing work's own use. R6 is coded as the residual. (3) C1 is borderline: the list pairs 'MBTI und 16Personalities' in the same slot where the neighbouring item reads 'DiSC beziehungsweise Everything DiSC' ('bzw.' = 'or rather'), which could be read as treating the pair as one instrument. 'und' is weaker than the parenthetical equations §7 uses as C1 exemplars, so C0 is coded conservatively; an adjudicator reading the pairing as an identity claim would code C1.
free_text: c1: The retrieved text is a repository abstract page, not the full article PDF. Per its own English abstract, the work is a critical narrative review comparing six assessment instruments: "the MBTI and 16Personalities, DiSC and Everything DiSC, the Big-Five model, the Enneagram, and Gallup CliftonStrengths" (Abstract (English)), alongside the author's own instrument, the "Job-Related Personality Test (Berufsbezogener Persönlichkeitstest, BPT)", whose validation with 31,373 professionals is stated to be documented in a separate book (Pelz, 2023), not in this work. No instrument is administered within this text, consistent with E4. The German and English abstract sentences list "MBTI und 16Personalities" / "the MBTI and 16Personalities" as two separate items under review (joined by "und"/"and"), rather than naming one as a form of the other, which is why no C1-C3 conflation flag was set from the available text. || c2: Not one of the three §7 calibration records. Two notes. (a) The Zenodo page gives the DOI as 10.5281/zenodo.21517802 ('DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21517802'), while the assigned DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.21517801 — consistent with Zenodo's concept-DOI/version-DOI pair; the title 'Persönlichkeitstests im beruflichen Kontext' matches the assignment, so this is taken to be the right work. (b) The abstract reports an administration to 31,373 people — 'Seine Entwicklung und Validierung mit 31.373 Fach- und Führungskräften ist in Persönlichkeit gewinnt dokumentiert (Pelz, 2023)' [English gloss: 'Its development and validation with 31,373 professionals and managers are documented in Persönlichkeit gewinnt (Pelz, 2023)'] — but that administration is of the author's own Berufsbezogener Persönlichkeitstest (BPT), not an MBTI-type instrument, and it is explicitly attributed to a prior publication rather than performed for this work, so it does not make this work E1.
